correctness.rationale: With unit increments and λ>0, the pre-event Poisson memory is finite almost surely by its finite mean λ/γ, and the reduced Palm past is an ordinary Poisson past. The Laplace functional and substitution u=κ exp(−γt) give the exponent −λJ(κ)/γ. For periodic arrivals it is the pre-jump geometric sum, not the uniform-phase arbitrary-time memory, that gives the exponent −κ/(exp(γ/λ)−1). Compensation and stationary intensity respectively give the two expected count rates; no independence between response marks is needed beyond the stipulated conditional mean and no feedback. The log ratio of the positive memory-dependent components has the sign of κh(γ/λ)−J(κ), and h(y)=y/(exp(y)−1) strictly decreases from 1 to 0 while 0<J/κ<1. This proves the unique crossing and both strict orderings. J/κ is strictly decreasing by its integral over [0,1]; its expansion 1−κ/4+O(κ²) and h(y)=1−y/2+O(y²) give the small-κ limit. For κ large, J=log κ+O(1) and h((1±ε)log κ) bracket J/κ since h(y)~ye^(−y). The derivative α+β(1−x)exp(−x), x=λJ/γ, has a unique minimum α−βe^(−2) and gives the claimed Lambert W zeros; equality gives an isolated horizontal tangent, not a decreasing interval. This is an expectation theorem for stipulated responses, not an empirical or sample-path claim. The frozen checker.py and VERIFICATION.md were inspected, not executed; quadrature, finite test cases and truncated-history simulations corroborate but do not prove the result.

value.rationale: The result gives a natural equal-intensity benchmark that distinguishes what happens at arrivals from what happens at arbitrary times, shows that neither schedule uniformly minimizes expected flight counts, and identifies exactly when increasing events paradoxically decreases expected total responses under the model. The asymptotics delineate the sensitivity range of the crossover. This is a useful exact model classification, not a validated ecological intervention or a new Laplace identity.
